questions.question: What is the difference between arrow functions and regular functions?
questions.title: Arrow Functions Vs Regular
questions.direct_answer: Three differences: (1) this — arrows have NO own this; they capture the enclosing scope's this lexically (defined where regular functions get theirs at call time by receiver). (2) arguments — arrows have no own arguments object (rest params replace it). (3) Form — arrows can't be constructors (no new), can't be generators, and support concise expression bodies. Regular functions: dynamic this, own arguments, usable as constructors.

sections.title: Interview Answer
Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    R[regular function] -->|this at CALL time| CT{who is the receiver?}
    CT -->|obj.method| O[obj]
    CT -->|plain call| U[undefined / global]
    CT -->|new| N[new instance]
    A[arrow function] -->|this at WRITE time| L[enclosing scope's this - captured forever]
    L --> CB[callbacks keep this: timers, map, then]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
Why arrows exist (the history that explains the design): pre-2015, keeping this across a callback required `const self = this` or `.bind(this)` — the #1 source of this-bugs. Arrows eliminated the entire bug class by removing this-binding from the function — the closure treats this like any other lexical name. The cost: arrows can NEVER have their this changed (bind/call/apply affect nothing this-related on arrows — they still run), which is exactly why they're wrong for methods that need a dynamic receiver and right for callbacks that must keep the writer's.

The class-field interaction (the modern gotcha): class fields defined as arrows (handleClick = () => {...}) pre-bind this to the instance — the pattern React class components used for event handlers. Methods (regular) on the prototype need binding at use sites. Function-components + hooks made this mostly moot — hooks-era React has no this at all, which is worth saying out loud: the framework moved away from this the same direction the language did.

The performance/spec corners (the honest depth): arrows and regular functions have no meaningful perf difference in modern engines (the old 'arrows are faster' claim is myth); function declarations are hoisted (usable before definition) while const arrow assignments hit the TDZ — a load-order bug class arrows introduced; and the exhaustive spec rule: an arrow's this is captured from its creation scope — module top level → undefined (strict) or globalThis (sloppy), inside a method → the method's receiver, inside another arrow → that arrow's captured this, unchanged all the way down.
